summary:
## Producer Price Surge Continues

May's producer price index climbed 0.8% month-over-month, marking the ninth consecutive month of increases. Year-over-year, prices jumped 8.5%, reaching the highest level in three years and ten months. Financial service fees, urban gas, and semiconductors drove the gains, though the monthly pace of increases has moderated. This represents the second-longest consecutive rise since November 2020, when prices climbed for thirteen straight months. Petroleum products showed slight declines, but chemical products and utility costs are emerging as new pressure points in the inflation picture.

## Inflation Outlook Remains Sticky

The Bank of Korea projects consumer inflation will settle around 3% in the second half of this year, with core inflation rising to the mid-2% range. Despite easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, inflation may prove difficult to contain due to sustained consumption growth and wage increases. Global commodity prices, particularly grains and livestock products, continue to rise, with fallout from the Ukraine conflict expected to persist for three to twelve months ahead. These pressures will likely filter into processed food and restaurant pricing before year-end.

## Record Current Account Surplus Masks Trade Shift

Korea recorded a historic current account surplus last year, yet the trade picture revealed significant shifts. The surplus with the United States contracted for the first time in six years due to tariff impacts, while the deficit with China widened to mark four consecutive years of red ink as steel exports declined. The 123 billion dollar overall current account surplus represents the nation's strongest position ever, reflecting robust exports despite narrowing trade advantages with key markets.

## Real Estate Heating in Seoul Periphery

Properties in Seoul's outer districts are attracting heavy demand from "2030" age group investors seeking affordable entry points. Jungrang District saw listings drop 12%, while Nowon District declined 8%, as renters convert to ownership amid housing shortages. The Sagajung Central I-Park complex in Jungrang's Myeongmok area posted record prices, with an 84 square-meter unit selling for 1.52 billion won in mid-May. Rising prices across new apartment developments signal renewed confidence in previously overlooked neighborhoods.

## Small Business Loan Restructuring Underway

The government announced a 2.2 trillion won restructuring of nonperforming small business loans while establishing 2 trillion won in new regional credit guarantee programs. This measure represents a comprehensive overhaul of the regional credit guarantee system aimed at stabilizing the small business sector. Combined with youth employment recovery initiatives and deregulation of subscription services, the government is broadening its economic stimulus footprint beyond traditional policy tools.

## Stock Market Reaches Historic Highs

The KOSPI index shattered records, surging past 9,300 points for the first time ever, driven entirely by semiconductor powerhouses Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. The index climbed 225.05 points, or 2.48%, reaching 9,288.89 at opening and rising further to 9,342.93 by mid-morning. Samsung Electronics hit 380,000 won per share while SK Hynix reached 2.8 million won, both record highs. However, the gains were heavily concentrated, with only 11% of KOSPI components advancing and the KOSDAQ index declining, revealing significant market divergence.

## Semiconductor ETF Surge Reflects AI Boom

The Shinhan Asset Management SOL AI Semiconductor Top 2 Plus exchange-traded fund surpassed 7 trillion won in net assets just three months after launch, demonstrating explosive appetite for semiconductor exposure. Meanwhile, Korea Investment Trust's Global Semiconductor Top 4 Plus ETF achieved 100,000 won per share for the first time, marking the fastest price appreciation among domestic semiconductor ETFs. These gains reflect broader enthusiasm for the sector amid global artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion.

## Global Memory Market Balloons Fourfold

The worldwide memory semiconductor market is projected to reach approximately 1.5 quadrillion won this year, expanding 4.2 times from last year's 360 trillion won. Server memory demand has emerged as the critical growth driver, with server applications expanding from 37% of total memory sales last year to an expected 56% this year. This explosive growth stems from North American data center investments supporting artificial intelligence model development and deployment across major technology firms.

## International Tourism Spending Surges

Foreign visitors spent a record 2.122 trillion won in Korea during May, surging 67% year-over-year and marking the first time monthly spending exceeded 2 trillion won. Chinese tourists led the rebound with spending tripling from the previous year, signaling restoration of key regional tourism flows. This spending surge demonstrates Korea's strengthening appeal as a destination amid global economic recovery and easing travel restrictions.

## Industrial Expansion Supports Semiconductor Growth

Lotte Chemical's subsidiaries are investing 130 billion won to establish a photoresist production facility in Pyeongtaek, producing high-purity materials essential for semiconductor and display manufacturing. This facility will enable vertical integration from raw materials through finished products. Only Korea, Japan, and the United States currently possess photoresist production capacity, with Lotte subsidiary Handuck Chemical ranking globally as the market leader.

## Energy Infrastructure Expansion Begins

The government selected Yeongdeok in Gyeongbuk Province as the site for two large-scale nuclear reactors and Gijang in Busan for one small modular reactor plant, marking Korea's first nuclear site selections in fifteen years. This decision reflects the government's dual-track energy strategy combining renewable sources with baseload nuclear power to support rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and electric vehicle proliferation. Nuclear construction is expected to begin within the current government term.

## Currency Weakness Persists Amid Fed Hawkishness

The Korean won traded around 1,530 per dollar, remaining elevated despite easing Middle East geopolitical risks. Hawkish Federal Reserve messaging and persistent global dollar demand pressure the currency lower. The won's weakness adds inflationary headwinds for import-dependent Korea while boosting export competitiveness, creating mixed implications for different economic sectors.

## Marina Industry Receives Government Support

The government announced comprehensive marina activation plans including improved port infrastructure and vessel identification systems modeled after automobile registration. These reforms aim to expand the marine leisure industry while enhancing market transparency and transaction efficiency. This initiative targets the growing affluent consumer segment seeking recreational watercraft experiences.

## Key Implications for Investors and Consumers

Today's economic picture reflects sharply divergent forces. While semiconductor stocks surge to historic highs on artificial intelligence infrastructure spending and memory market expansion, most Korean consumers remain financially stressed. Renters face mounting deposit costs as Seoul property prices climb, with nationwide housing affordability deteriorating despite government restructuring efforts. Producer price pressures persist through chemical and utility costs, suggesting sticky inflation despite geopolitical improvement. The Bank of Korea's projection of 3% year-end inflation confirms these pressures. Investors should recognize that semiconductor concentration creates market fragility—with only two major stocks driving national indices higher while broader participation weakens. The won's currency weakness supports exporters but increases living costs for ordinary households. Government stimulus targeting small businesses and expanded nuclear capacity signal confidence in longer-term growth, yet near-term consumer affordability challenges remain acute. For individual investors, the divergence between benchmark performance and typical stock performance presents a cautionary tale about diversification risk.
headline: Producer Prices Rise Nine Months Straight, Markets Hit Record Highs on Semiconductor Rally
